items.text: Prepare a framework, not a news list: security, economy, international order, and transnational problems; use historical case studies to show how national interest, domestic politics and alliances interact.
Do not convert this topic into a random list of current news items.
Do not assume U.S. values and U.S. strategic interests always point in the same direction.
Do not use present-day priorities for every historical period; concerns change over time.
U.S. foreign policy has long combined security, economic and ideological interests.
Middle Eastern policy has involved energy, Israel, Arab partners, Iran and counterterrorism in changing combinations.
Climate, cyber threats and global health illustrate problems military power alone cannot manage.
Use the category framework (security, economy, international order, transnational problems) rather than attempting to list every issue chronologically.
U.S. values and U.S. strategic interests do not always align — a tension worth naming explicitly rather than assuming automatic consistency.
